skill.name: seedance-v2
skill.description: Generate 4 to 15 second cinematic videos with ByteDance Seedance 2.0 Pro through RunComfy. The skill guides prompt design, reference media use, lip-sync settings, and RunComfy CLI invocation for short-form video generation.
skill.summary: Generate short cinematic Seedance 2.0 Pro videos with RunComfy CLI guidance.
skill.author: agentspace-so

security_audit.summary: The skill is a transparent RunComfy CLI guide for Seedance 2.0 Pro video generation. Most static findings are false positives from Markdown backticks, placeholder URLs, and documentation formatting; confirmed risks are intentional CLI execution, outbound RunComfy API use, generated-file downloads, and local token storage.

remediation.issue: External CLI execution is central to the skill.
remediation.suggestion: Keep command examples explicit, avoid shell interpolation, and require users to review prompts, media URLs, and output paths before running the CLI.

remediation.issue: RunComfy authentication stores a service token locally.
remediation.suggestion: Document token rotation, least-privilege account use, and CI preference for short-lived RUNCOMFY_TOKEN secrets where available.

remediation.issue: Generated outputs are downloaded from remote URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Continue restricting downloads to RunComfy hosts and keep file size limits to reduce disk-fill and untrusted-download risk.

content.value_statement: Short video generation often needs precise prompt structure, reference media, and model-specific limits. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through Seedance 2.0 Pro setup, inputs, and safe RunComfy CLI use.
actual_capabilities: Explains when Seedance 2.0 Pro is the right model for cinematic short-form video.
Documents the RunComfy CLI command for the bytedance/seedance-v2/pro endpoint.
Describes supported prompt, image, video, audio, aspect ratio, duration, resolution, audio, and seed inputs.
Gives practical prompt guidance for camera motion, lip-sync tone, ambience, and identity preservation.
Compares Seedance 2.0 Pro with related models for routing decisions.
Documents basic RunComfy authentication, exit codes, endpoints, and output download behavior.
limitations: The endpoint only supports 4 to 15 second clips.
The documented playground variant is limited to 720p output.
Reference video and audio inputs must be 2 to 15 seconds, with audio under 15 MB.
The skill depends on the local RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and outbound network access.

use_cases.title: Create dialogue ads
use_cases.description: Produce short spokesperson or product clips with native audio and lip-sync guidance.

use_cases.title: Prototype cinematic scenes
use_cases.description: Turn a shot brief, image reference, and motion direction into a RunComfy-ready video generation request.

use_cases.title: Test branded video variants
use_cases.description: Use fixed prompts, reference images, aspect ratios, and seeds to compare short-form creative variants.

prompt_templates.title: Basic text-to-video clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a simple clip
prompt_templates.prompt: Use Seedance 2.0 Pro to create a 5 second 9:16 video of a calm product reveal. Include camera motion, lighting, mood, and audio direction.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-synced spokesperson
prompt_templates.scenario: Use an image reference for identity stability
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Seedance 2.0 Pro prompt for an 8 second spokesperson ad using one character image. The person should say a short launch message with warm natural delivery.

prompt_templates.title: Multimodal scene with references
prompt_templates.scenario: Combine image, video, and audio references
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare a RunComfy Seedance 2.0 Pro request using one subject image, one scene video, and one voice reference. Keep the output within model limits.

prompt_templates.title: Model routing and production plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Decide whether Seedance 2.0 Pro is the best model for this brief. Compare it with HappyHorse, Wan, and Kling, then provide the recommended RunComfy command plan.

output_examples.input: A marketer asks for a vertical cafe spokesperson ad with a headshot reference.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends Seedance 2.0 Pro, drafts a concise lip-sync prompt, sets 9:16 and 8 seconds, and explains where to place the image reference.

output_examples.input: A filmmaker asks for a cinematic previs shot using a scene clip and voice reference.
output_examples.output: The skill structures the prompt around subject, camera motion, ambience, and reference media, while keeping video and audio inputs inside duration limits.

output_examples.input: A user asks for a 30 second Seedance video.
output_examples.output: The skill explains the 15 second maximum and suggests splitting the concept into multiple shorter clips.

best_practices: Use image references for stable identity, costumes, logos, or product appearance.
Put changing action, camera movement, lighting, mood, and speech direction in the prompt.
Match reference media aspect ratio and duration to the target output when possible.
anti_patterns: Do not ask for clips longer than 15 seconds in one request.
Do not mix conflicting visual styles unless the contrast is intentional.
Do not rely on text alone to preserve a specific face or brand mark.

faq.question: What does this skill help me do?
faq.answer: It helps you prepare Seedance 2.0 Pro video generation requests for RunComfy, including prompts, references, and CLI usage.

faq.question: Does it generate videos directly inside Claude?
faq.answer: No. It guides Claude, Codex, or Claude Code to use the local RunComfy CLI and RunComfy model API.

faq.question: What inputs can Seedance 2.0 Pro use?
faq.answer: It can use a text prompt, up to 9 images, up to 3 short videos, and up to 3 short audio references.

faq.question: How long can the generated video be?
faq.answer: The documented endpoint supports whole-second durations from 4 to 15 seconds.

faq.question: Can it create lip-synced dialogue?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill focuses on native in-pass audio and lip-sync guidance for short dialogue and spokesperson clips.

faq.question: What should I review before running it?
faq.answer: Review the prompt, reference URLs, output directory, token handling, and any generated files downloaded from RunComfy.
